messages.content: I received the Boba Fett but there's more paint wear than described, especially on the knee joints. Also, the blaster doesn't look like an original Kenner piece to me — the plastic texture is wrong.

There is no paint wear beyond what's described in the listing. What you're seeing on the knee joints is surface texture variation from the original manufacturing process — vintage Kenner figures have uneven paint application on articulation points. The blaster is 100% original Kenner — I have a professional authentication certificate confirming all components are authentic and condition consistent with the listing.

The listing specifically said '95%+ paint intact' and only mentioned the helmet visor. The knee wear should have been disclosed separately. And I'd like to see the authentication certificate — I've been collecting for 15 years and the blaster texture is off compared to my other originals.

I'll submit the authentication certificate and provenance documentation as evidence. Kenner had production variations — not every blaster from 1979 will look identical. My authenticator confirmed everything is genuine and condition matches the listing. The 95% paint assessment is accurate — the buyer is confusing normal manufacturing texture with paint loss.
I'll review what you submit. But undisclosed paint wear and a questionable blaster on a $900 figure is a significant issue regardless of what a certificate says.
